ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The shapes conforming to the golden ratio \( \left(\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}\right) \) are often visually pleasing. In the pentagram shown, where \( AD=BC=\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2} \), and both points C and D are the golden sections of \( AB \), what is the length of \( CD \)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that points C and D are both golden section points of AB,\\
hence $AC=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB$, $BD=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB$,\\
thus $AC+BD=AB+CD$,\\
which means $AC+BD=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB+\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB=(\sqrt{5}-1)AB=AB+CD$,\\
$AB=\frac{CD}{\sqrt{5}-2}=(\sqrt{5}+2)CD$,\\
since $AB=AD+BD+CD=\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}AB+\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}AB+CD=\sqrt{5}+1+CD$,\\
thus $(\sqrt{5}+2)CD=\sqrt{5}+1+CD$,\\
therefore $(\sqrt{5}+1)CD=\sqrt{5}+1$,\\
solving this gives $CD=\boxed{1}$.

ready3_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The shapes conforming to the golden ratio \(\left(\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}\right)\) are often visually pleasing. In the pentagram shown, where \(AD=BC=\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}\), and both points C and D are the golden sections of \(AB\), what is the length of \(CD\)?
ready3_open_rewrite.raw_answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that points C and D are both golden section points of AB,\\
hence $AC=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB$, $BD=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB$,\\
thus $AC+BD=AB+CD$,\\
which means $AC+BD=\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB+\frac{\sqrt{5}-1}{2}AB=(\sqrt{5}-1)AB=AB+CD$,\\
$AB=\frac{CD}{\sqrt{5}-2}=(\sqrt{5}+2)CD$,\\
since $AB=AD+BD+CD=\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}AB+\frac{\sqrt{5}+1}{2}AB+CD=\sqrt{5}+1+CD$,\\
thus $(\sqrt{5}+2)CD=\sqrt{5}+1+CD$,\\
therefore $(\sqrt{5}+1)CD=\sqrt{5}+1$,\\
solving this gives $CD=\boxed{1}$
